name: input.keyboard.key
description: Press a virtual key by name (atomic press-release). Pass `duration_ms` to control the press-to-release gap (capped at 1000ms; longer holds use `input.keyboard.key_down` + `input.keyboard.key_up`). For ctrl-X / shift-X / alt-X chords, use `modifiers`. Synthesised keystrokes deliver via the user32 layer only; targets that read the kernel keyboard table directly (DirectInput, RawInput, `GetAsyncKeyState`) — including Unity and most game frameworks — won't observe them. See `spec/operators/05-footguns.md` for the capability boundary.

vk.description: Key name. Common keys: `enter`, `tab`, `escape`, `space`, `backspace`, `delete`, `home`, `end`, `pageup`, `pagedown`, arrow keys (`up`/`down`/`left`/`right`), function keys (`F1`-`F24`), single characters (`a`-`z`, `0`-`9`, punctuation). Case-insensitive.

duration_ms.description: Optional press-to-release gap in milliseconds (0-1000). Default = OS-minimum (a regular fast keypress). Useful for slow-press-detection workflows. Cap is 1 second; the verb is synchronous and longer holds belong on `input.keyboard.key_down` + `input.keyboard.key_up`.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the key press. Each is synthesised down before, up after.

x-output-schema.description: Empty body — wire response is the literal `OK 0`. The focused window receives the key event; no target-confirmation field (use `window.focus` first if a specific target matters).

x-implementations.name: send_input
x-implementations.description: Win32 `SendInput` with INPUT_KEYBOARD events. Modifier-down events bracket the vk press-release. Vk names map to Win32 VK_* constants via the agent's name table. When `duration_ms > 0`, the agent issues the down event, sleeps via the request thread for the requested interval, then issues the up event — the connection is wedged for the duration.

x-implementations.name: keybd_event
x-implementations.description: Win32 `keybd_event` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x where `SendInput` is unavailable.

windows-modern.description: SendInput INPUT_KEYBOARD events. Reaches user32 message-queue listeners (most apps). Does NOT reach RawInput / DirectInput targets — Unity, DirectX games, and apps using `GetAsyncKeyState` against the kernel keyboard table will not see these events. The verb returns `OK` because user32 accepts the events; the in-target effect is silently nil. See dist/PROTOCOL.md §4.4 for the empirical chain (issue #64). UIPI applies: synthesised input to higher-IL windows is silently dropped — agent detects via post-press `GetForegroundWindow` mismatch. `duration_ms` adds a Sleep between the down and up events; the call is synchronous so the connection blocks for that long.

windows-classic.description: SendInput on NT 5+; keybd_event on NT 4 / 9x. Same RawInput / DirectInput limitation applies (the Interception driver workaround is also classic-compatible if installed). No UIPI on NT 4 / 9x / 2000. `duration_ms` behaves the same as on modern.
